Academic papers are necessarily compact and specialized. Important engineering ideas can therefore be difficult to see behind the equations, methodology, and technical details.

**Research Explained** revisits published research from a broader perspective: the engineering problem, the underlying physical or conceptual idea, the method used to address it, and what the results mean in practice.

## Research areas

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [Offshore & Ocean Engineering](research/offshore-ocean-engineering.qmd)

Offshore wind structures, floating systems, wave-energy devices, structural flexibility, and the mechanics behind offshore response.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [Concrete & Materials](research/concrete-materials.qmd)

Concrete durability, reactive particles, industrial by-products, material deterioration, and the mechanics connecting microstructure to engineering performance.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [Engineering Decisions](research/engineering-decisions.qmd)

Decision frameworks for engineering problems, including bias reduction, factor structure, weighting, and evidence-based comparison.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [Computational Mechanics & Fracture](research/computational-mechanics-fracture.qmd)

XFEM, XEFG, multiple cracks, alternative crack representations, multiscale fracture, and the broader lessons of enriched computational mechanics.
:::
:::
